title: Kolkata puts 3,700 police on Chhath duty at 163 ghats; Rabindra Sarobar stays shut
dek: With the Chorbagan crowd crush still fresh, the city has posted five extra IPS officers, 158 patrol teams and divers at the ghats, and kept devotees out of the two south Kolkata lakes under the green tribunal's ban.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Kolkata Police have deployed more than 3,700 personnel at the city's river ghats, ponds and lakes for Chhath Puja, with the city on guard against crowding at the water's edge after 19 people died in a crowd crush at a Durga Puja pandal in Chorbagan.

Five IPS officers from the West Bengal Police have been attached to Kolkata Police for the festival, and 35 senior officers will supervise security and surveillance across the city, according to reports. Entry to Rabindra Sarobar and Subhas Sarobar, the two south Kolkata lakes where the festival was once held in large numbers, remains barred under an order of the National Green Tribunal, and about 300 additional police have been posted around them to keep people out.

## The arrangements

The Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) and the Kolkata Metropolitan Development Authority (KMDA) have prepared 163 ghats for the festival, including 30 on the banks of the Ganga, two on the Adi Ganga, 86 at ponds and other water bodies, and six artificial ponds, according to reports. Civil Defence volunteers, the police disaster management force and divers are to be stationed at every major ghat, with boats and speedboats patrolling the river. Watch towers, public address systems, helplines, medical teams and bio-toilets have been set up, and the KMC has put up QR codes that people can scan for information on the arrangements.

To stop the use of banned firecrackers and loud music from DJ systems, 158 special police teams will patrol the ghats.

Kolkata Police have also announced traffic restrictions. Goods vehicles are barred from city roads from noon to 10 pm on Sunday, 15 November, and from 3 am to 10 am on Monday, 16 November. Parking, picking up and dropping passengers, and loading and unloading are banned on 53 roads, among them Dufferin Road, Bidhan Sarani, Vivekananda Road, Red Road and Khidirpur Road, according to reports.

## Why the scrutiny

The Chorbagan crush, at a north Kolkata pandal during Durga Puja, killed 19 people and injured at least 25. Afterwards the state government issued safety rules for Kali Puja, Jagaddhatri Puja and Chhath, telling organisers to keep pandals well lit, widen entry and exit routes and control the flow of visitors, after officials said dim theme lighting had hindered crowd management at Chorbagan. Chhath, with large crowds gathering at the water's edge before dusk and dawn, adds the risk of drowning to that of crowding.

## The lakes

The lakes have been at the centre of an argument for years. The National Green Tribunal barred the festival at Rabindra Sarobar to protect the lake's ecology, and the ban has repeatedly been tested by devotees and politicians. Earlier this month the state's Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Minister, Agnimitra Paul, first said the government would allow Chhath at Rabindra Sarobar this year, then said two days later that it would not be held there without the tribunal's permission, and promised at least 50 alternative ghats in south Kolkata. No change to the tribunal's order has been announced.

## What happens next

The goods-vehicle ban ends at 10 am on Monday, 16 November, the last day of the festival. The tribunal's order on the two lakes remains in force.
